```{=typst}
// === PAGE ===
#set page(
  paper: "a4",
  fill: rgb("#F8F7F0"),
  margin: (top: 0.9in, bottom: 0.5in, left: 1in, right: 1in),
  footer: context {
    set text(size: 8pt, fill: rgb("#666"), style: "italic")
    let updated = datetime.today().display(
      "Updated [month repr:long] [day padding:none], [year]"
    )
    grid(
      columns: (1fr, 1fr, 1fr),
      align(left)[#updated],
      align(center)[Page #counter(page).display() of #counter(page).final().last()],
      align(right)[#link("https://pingfan.org")[pingfan.org]],
    )
  },
)

#set text(font: ("Optima", "Helvetica Neue", "Arial"), size: 11pt)
#set par(leading: 0.55em, justify: false, spacing: 0pt)
#set block(spacing: 0pt)

// === SPACING KNOBS ===
#let gap = 5pt
#let entry-gap = 3pt

// === LISTS & TABLES ===
#show list: set block(spacing: 0.4em)
#show list: set par(leading: 0.45em)
// a bullet is a short gray hairline, a number gray Maple Mono with its
// period, as on the site
#let list-mark = box(height: 0.66em, width: 0.5em, place(horizon, line(length: 0.5em, stroke: 0.6pt + rgb("#A3A096"))))
#let enum-mark(n) = text(font: "Maple Mono NF", size: 0.8em, fill: rgb("#77746B"))[#n.]
#set list(indent: 1em, body-indent: 0.5em, marker: list-mark, spacing: 0.5em)

#show enum: set block(spacing: 0.4em)
#show enum: set par(leading: 0.45em)
#set enum(indent: 1em, body-indent: 0.5em, spacing: 0.5em, numbering: enum-mark)

#show list: it => { it; v(gap) }
#show enum: it => { it; v(gap) }
#show table: it => { v(3pt); it; v(gap) }

// Navy-blue links
#show link: set text(fill: rgb(0%, 20%, 60%))

// The research chunk shared with the About page (resources/chunks/research.qmd)
// arrives as headings over paragraphs: a heading is set like a lettered
// subsection (A., B., C., as the other sections letter theirs), and a link
// into the site (Quarto writes its path as ./research/...) is pointed at
// pingfan.org.
#show heading: it => block(above: 8pt, below: 4pt,
  text(size: 11pt, weight: "bold")[#counter(heading).display(it.numbering) #it.body])
#show link: it => if type(it.dest) == str and it.dest.starts-with("./") { link("https://pingfan.org" + it.dest.slice(1), it.body) } else { it }

// === HELPERS ===
// A mark from the site's glyph map (resources/styles/styles.scss), read at
// compile time so the documents and the page share one drawing: gray, at
// the size of the text, its center 0.29em above the baseline, between the
// lowercase and capital centers, as the page's marks and the skill marks.
#let glyph(name, size: 0.9em) = {
  let scss = read("resources/styles/styles.scss")
  let svg = scss.match(regex("\n  \"" + name + "\": \"(<svg[^\"]*</svg>)\"")).captures.at(0)
  box(width: size, height: 0.58em, place(horizon + center, image(bytes(svg.replace("'black'", "'#77746B'")), height: size)))
}

// Section header with underline rule. Sticky so it never strands at a page bottom.
#let section(name) = block(sticky: true)[
  #text(size: 12pt, weight: "bold")[#upper[#name]]
  #v(5pt)
  #line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.5pt + rgb("#888"))
  #v(gap)
]

// Subsection header - bold, no rule.
#let subsection(name) = {
  text(size: 11pt, weight: "bold")[#name]
  v(4pt)
}

// === HEADER ===
#align(center)[
  #text(size: 18pt)[Pingfan Hu]
]

#v(6pt)

#align(center)[
  Engineering Management and Systems Engineering
]

#v(2pt)

#align(center)[
  The George Washington University, Washington, DC, USA
]

#v(10pt)

#align(center)[
  // each mark inline before its text, so it sits in the text's own line
  // (a mark in a cell of its own is centered on the row, not on the words)
  #grid(
    columns: 1,
    row-gutter: 3pt,
    align: left,
    [#glyph("map-pin")~Greater Melbourne, Australia],
    [#glyph("phone")~+61 431 251 227],
    [#glyph("mail")~#link("mailto:pingfanhu@proton.me")[pingfanhu\@proton.me]],
    [#glyph("compass")~#link("https://pingfan.org")[pingfan.org]],
  )
]

#v(10pt)

#section[Education]

#align(center)[
  #table(
    columns: (auto, auto, auto, auto),
    stroke: none,
    inset: (x: 0pt, y: 2pt),
    column-gutter: 10pt,
    align: left,
    [2026], [*George Washington University*, Washington, D.C.], [Ph.D.], [Systems Engineering],
    table.cell(colspan: 4)[#pad(left: 0.5em)[#text(size: 9.5pt)[Dissertation: _Sustainable Transportation, Sustainable Research: Consumer Adoption and Grid Peak-Shaving of Battery Electric Vehicle Smart Charging, Inspiring the surveydown Open-Source Survey Platform_]]],
    table.cell(colspan: 4)[#h(0.5em)#text(size: 9.5pt)[Doctoral Committee: _John Paul Helveston, Caitlin Grady, Johan René van Dorp, & Eric Hittinger_]],
    table.cell(colspan: 4)[#h(0.5em)#text(size: 9.5pt)[Dissertation defended; degree conferral expected December 2026.]],
    [2018], [*University of Sydney*, Sydney, NSW, Australia], [M.P.E.], [Mechanical Engineering],
    [2015], [*Pennsylvania State University*, State College, PA], [B.S.], [Industrial Engineering],
  )
]

#v(5pt)

#section[Research Interests]
// a heading steps the counter only when it has a numbering; the function
// letters by the heading's own level alone, since the levels above it are zero
#set heading(numbering: (..n) => numbering("A.", n.pos().last()))
// its paragraphs stand in from the margin as the lists' text does (the
// list indent, its marker and its body indent); the brackets keep the rule
// to the chunk
#[
#show par: it => pad(left: 2em, it)
```

#section[Industry Experiences]

- Co-Founder of _Alkaline Software_, an app development studio founded with Professor John Paul Helveston that builds apps in Rust with GPUI. Lead developer of the flagship product Emaki, an Agentic Development Environment (ADE). #link("https://github.com/alkaline-software")[github.com/alkaline-software]. Remote (2026 - Present).

- Project Engineer at _GE Appliances_. Participated in GE's Edison Engineering Development Program with various appliance projects, showing expertise in PLM management and designs. Qingdao, China (2019 - 2020).
- Assistant Process Engineer (Intern) at _Kurtz Ersa GmbH_. Executed a DoE for new soldering technology, and featured as lead actor in Ersa's first Asian market promotion video on YouTube. Wertheim, Germany (Jan. - Mar. 2017).
